label: WorkBuddy
notes: Tencent CodeBuddy Code (genie). This desktop build ships only the headless bundle, so `/login` cannot run from it; the account session was established with the full npm distribution (@tencent-ai/codebuddy-code) launched against THIS install's product.json, and both binaries share the resulting stored session. CRITICAL: the CLI takes its whole product identity from ACC_PRODUCT_CONFIG_PATH (see run.env). The identical relative path inside the npm package holds a CodeBuddy config (www.codebuddy.ai), and the same binary then rejects a WorkBuddy account with 'Authentication required' — which is why discovery ignores PATH and accepts only this install's own entry. Output is a JSON ARRAY of events whose last element is the result. 2026-10-15 LAYOUT CHANGE: the app update replaced cli/dist/* with the lite bundle `dist/codebuddy-lite-wb.mjs`, and the old `bin/codebuddy` launcher now fails in print mode with "Cannot find module '../dist/codebuddy'" (its headless bundle is gone). Discovery therefore PREFERS the .mjs entry, which supports both --version and -p, and keeps bin/codebuddy only as a fallback for older installs. Credentials: the CLI accepts CODEBUDDY_AUTH_TOKEN / CODEBUDDY_API_KEY from the environment, but its own stored session is encrypted and this plugin never reads or writes it. The run environment additionally blanks CODEBUDDY_AUTH_TOKEN: this plugin reads that variable itself (balance probe), but forwarding it makes the CLI treat it as its own credential, and any non-Latin1 value then kills *every run* before a request leaves — observed as the runtime's "Cannot convert argument to a ByteString" error, with a perfectly valid stored login sitting behind it.

balance.note: WorkBuddy's balance endpoints answer for an account API key, and issuing one needs a paid membership, so on a free account there is nothing this plugin can read — the row stays hidden instead of showing an error the user cannot act on. To turn it back on: set kind to "http" and restore base/probe/summary (https://www.workbuddy.cn, GET /console/accounts picking data.accounts, POST /v2/billing/meter/get-user-resource-summary, map ResourceId/PackageName/total/used, unit 积分), then set CODEBUDDY_AUTH_TOKEN to a pure-ASCII key. lib/balance.js refuses a non-ASCII credential with a readable message rather than letting the runtime's ByteString error escape — and note that the same bad variable also breaks *runs*, because the plugin hands the environment to the CLI and the CLI tries to use it as a credential.

safety.note: Runs headless with -p. No permission-bypass flag is declared, so the CLI keeps its own prompts. The account token is read from the environment; this plugin never stores or writes one.
